summary: The ancient materials, occupational props and High Priest’s twin sun emblems work well. The four everyday roles are distinguishable, but several garments read as modern separates or rigid boards rather than wrapped cloth. The trader needs a stronger outsider identity at stream scale.
problems: Water Carrier, Village Elder and High Priest have straight, separately boxed lower legs that read as trousers rather than long wraps or robes. The Water Carrier’s square neckline and contrasting chest patch reinforce a tank-top impression.
The Reed Weaver’s bundle emerges directly behind the head like an oversized reed crown. Its carrying attachment is unclear, while the diagonal wrap reads as a rigid slab.
The Village Elder’s symmetrical front panels resemble a vest with a square collar rather than a broad wool shawl. This weakens the Bronze Age garment language despite the appropriate staff.

The trader’s striped mantle forms a long, straight board over one leg. The headwrap and stripes establish some difference, but the variable clothing colours overlap the villagers, and much of the balance scale disappears against the body.
Fine edging, small beads and narrow colour strips contribute little at stream size. The strongest recognition currently comes from props rather than garment construction.
fix: Water Carrier: Keep the head jar, but make its support pad visible and add a dark recessed mouth. Replace the square shirt neckline and chest patch with a continuous one-shoulder linen drape. Give the lower wrap an offset overlap and uneven hem rather than two rectangular trouser legs. Field Tender: Preserve the hoe and shorter tunic silhouette. Extend the sun cloth visibly down the back and sides, and add an overlapping tunic hem so the lower garment does not read as shorts; keep the shaft seated in the hand. Reed Weaver: Shift the sheaf behind one shoulder, with asymmetric tips clear of the head silhouette. Add a visible shoulder harness connected to the bundle’s lashings. Fit the diagonal cloth against the torso and narrow its projecting edges. Village Elder: Replace the vest-like front with a broad, asymmetric shawl crossing the chest and continuing over the shoulders; use a chunky contrasting woven border. Add an offset ankle-wrap closure. High Priest: Retain the tall sun staff, large pectoral and cream/turquoise palette. Rework the lower robe into overlapping, staggered panels and broaden the shoulder colour area for overhead recognition. River Trader: Establish a fixed deep-blue, ochre and cream textile palette distinct from the villagers. Shorten and step the mantle’s hanging edge, fit it closely to the torso and thigh, and place the balance farther outside the body silhouette so both pans read. Across all kits: eliminate exposed default-shirt edging. Keep upper wraps hip-bound and moving lower panels attached to their respective legs; do not solve the robe silhouette with one rigid piece spanning both limbs. Check shoulder, hem and prop clearance in walking poses at the actual stream camera.
